findings.evidence: ':203 Then check it: `python3 .claude/hooks/debate-status.py --json | jq '.topics[] | select(.topic=="<topic>") | .problems'`. Fix each problem it lists.' For a stale verdict debate-status.py skips the content checks: ':383 vp, derived = ([], None) if stale else verdict_problems(...)'. Reproduced: verdict with request_sha 0000000000000000 -> `.problems` = [] while status = stale and `--check` exits 2. No re-check is asked for after step 8 (promote), and the DoD (:282) relies on 'debate-status.py lists no problem for it'.
findings.problem: An arbitrator that mis-copies REQUEST_SHA (a 16-hex string handed over in a prompt) sees an empty problem list and returns COMPLETE; the verdict is stale from birth and the gate blocks. Likewise a skipped or failed `remember.sh decide` in step 8 is never re-checked, because the only check runs before step 8 and reads `.problems`, where 'not promoted' never appears.
findings.fix: Make the check `jq '.topics[]|select(.topic=="<t>")|{status,problems}'` and require status `resolved` and no problems; repeat it after step 8 reading `.gate` as well (empty except, for a close HIGH call, the expected second-opinion entry).

findings.evidence: forbidden ':57 "pattern": "a debate child spawned without run_in_background: false"' while the moderator (:104-111) and the trajectory step at :11 say 'where offered'. findings.problem: An interactive /eval run in which the moderator behaves exactly as instructed is scored as a forbidden trajectory, so the eval can't be run interactively and penalizes correct behaviour.
findings.fix: Change the pattern to 'a debate child spawned without run_in_background: false where the Agent tool offers it'.

findings.evidence: ':540 Analysis Paralysis Guard (applies to ALL agents spawned by this command)' ':542 If an agent makes 5+ consecutive read-only tool calls ... the agent MUST: Stop exploring'. Exception (:553) names only backend_audit_agent and ui_audit_agent. The arbitrator must read up to 4 briefs, 4 arguments, the protocol, PROJECT_FACTS, DECISIONS and re-fetch a source before its first write; a researcher makes up to 10 searches plus internal reads.
findings.problem: If a /develop parent passes this guard on to debate work (it says ALL agents), a researcher stops after five reads and an arbitrator writes a verdict before reading every argument, the opposite of what their prompts require. A countable limit that doesn't fit the job.
findings.fix: Add the debate agents (and other read-heavy judges) to the exception list.

findings.evidence: Step 1 (:74-76) validates only what debate-status.py lists: 'unreadable JSON, fewer than 2 options, no domain, a topic that isn't a slug'. debate-status.py request_problems (:160-161) only checks that `domain` is one of the six names. debate-protocol.md:98-100: '`domain` ... picks the rubric below, so set it honestly: auth, tokens, crypto, PII, CORS/CSRF, rate limits and tenant isolation are `security`.' Every security protection keys on that field: the security rubric (security_posture 35), `hardened_default` (arbitrator :153-158), the person gate on INCOMPLETE/disagreement (debate-status.py :467-470), the 'security debate' gate tag (:427). The domain is chosen by the requesting agent, which may already have built its default (`default_taken`).
findings.problem: A request about, say, rate-limit strategy or session TTL labelled `operations` or `architecture` is judged on a rubric with no security criterion, needs no hardened default, and never reaches the person gate; under /autonomous a permissive option can ship with no human seeing it. Nothing between the requester and the arbitrator checks that the label fits; the judge is handed a rubric chosen by an interested party.
findings.fix: Add to moderator step 1: if the decision, context or option labels touch the protocol's security list (auth, tokens, crypto, PII, CORS/CSRF, rate limits, tenant isolation) and `domain` isn't `security`, return `BLOCKED <topic>: request: domain should be security (<matched term>)`. Optionally mirror it as a keyword warning in debate-status.py request_problems.

findings.evidence: ':222 It prints `D-NNN recorded`. Put that id in the verdict as "decision_id".' No check for an existing entry. remember.sh decide (:71-100) always appends a new id; it doesn't look for an active block with the same link. Reproduced in scratch: running the documented decide command twice with `--link agent_state/debates/t5.verdict.json` prints 'D-001 recorded' then 'D-002 recorded'; DECISIONS.md has two `status: active` blocks with the same link. The moderator re-spawns an arbitrator that returns a progress note (debate_moderator.md:155 'Check its return as in step 4') and the parent may re-spawn the whole moderator (AI-10).
findings.problem: An arbitrator that ran step 8 and then ended its turn with a progress note is re-spawned, re-judges, and records a second active ledger entry for the same topic. If the re-judgment differs, the ledger holds two active, contradictory decisions; the SessionStart hook shows both to every session, and the gate's promoted() check (debate-status.py:306-311) passes because decision_id's block links to the verdict.
findings.fix: Before step 8: 'If an active DECISIONS.md block already links to this verdict, reuse its id (and if your decision differs, record yours with --reverses that id).' Better, make remember.sh decide refuse a second active entry with the same --link.

findings.evidence: Step 10 table (:201-205) keys the first line on status + `problems`: '`resolved`, no problems -> COMPLETE'; '`invalid` -> BLOCKED'. No row for `pending` or `stale`. Step 1 (:81) 'Already resolved (a valid, current verdict exists): return it as is. Don't re-run the debate.' But debate-status.py puts several gate failures in `gate`, not `problems`: unpromoted verdict (:464-466), invalid second opinion when one is needed (:449-450), security INCOMPLETE/disagreement (:467-470); and a stale verdict gets status `stale` with problems [] (:383). Reproduced in scratch: make_debate.py --no-promote -> `{status: resolved, problems: [], gate: ["... has no D-NNN in docs/DECISIONS.md ..."]}`, `--check` exit 2; a same-order second opinion -> `{status: resolved, problems: [], gate: ["second opinion didn't read the options in the reverse presentation order"]}`, `--check` exit 2; mis-copied request_sha -> `{status: stale, problems: [], gate: [...]}`, `--check` exit 2.
findings.problem: The moderator returns `COMPLETE <topic>` for a debate the gate will block (arbitrator forgot remember.sh, second opinion in the wrong order, request_sha mis-copied). The parent relaunches the requester and moves on. At the gate, Layer 0c (develop-orchestrator.md:1224) spawns the moderator again; step 1 sees a resolved verdict with no problems and returns it as is, so the topic never gets promoted or re-judged and the gate stays blocked with no defined way out. Under /autonomous this is a stall that needs a human. The moderator's DoD (:285) says its first line matches debate-status.py, but the check it runs can't see these cases.
findings.fix: In step 10 (and step 1's 'already resolved' test) read the topic's `gate` list too, e.g. `debate-status.py --json | jq '.topics[]|select(.topic=="<t>")|{status,problems,gate}'`: COMPLETE only when status is resolved and `gate` is empty. Add rows: `gate` says not promoted -> spawn the arbitrator with MODE: promote; second-opinion problem -> re-spawn the second opinion once; `stale` right after arbitration -> re-spawn the arbitrator with the correct REQUEST_SHA; `pending` (no verdict after re-spawns) -> `BLOCKED <topic>: verdict: arbitrator produced none`.

findings.evidence: The shuffle (:94) reorders ids, but the ids themselves keep request order: protocol :96 'ids A-D'; file names research-<id>.md / argument-<id>.md; the arbitrator sees 'PRESENTATION ORDER: B A C'. Requesters typically list their preferred option first (A).
findings.problem: General LLM-as-judge practice reports a label preference (towards 'A' or the first-listed id) separate from reading position. The shuffle hides the reading order but not which option the requester listed first.
findings.fix: Have the moderator hand the arbitrator neutral aliases (e.g. labels only, or a fresh letter mapping recorded in the transcript), mapping back in the verdict; or note the residual risk and test it in T-007.

findings.evidence: researcher and advocate `effort: medium` (Opus 5.5 default per platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort: 'medium ... The default on Claude Opus 5.5'); arbitrator `high`. T-007 checks research quality only by 'grep:http' in one brief (expected_artifacts.json:34-38). The Opus 5.5 guide: 'test several levels against your own evals'.
findings.problem: The settings are reasonable, but nothing would show whether research effort matters: an effort change on the researcher or advocate can't move any T-007 score except through the verdict label.
findings.fix: Add a rubric item that scores the briefs, e.g. the decisive claim in claims_checked is 'confirmed' (not contradicted) and every web row has a version/date, so /eval --compare can see an effort change.

findings.evidence: ':82-83 An active docs/DECISIONS.md entry already decides it under another topic: return BLOCKED ..., unless the request cites new evidence against it.' PRIOR DECISION is passed only for a stale verdict on the same topic (:84-86); arbitrator :83-85 adds --reverses only when given PRIOR DECISION.
findings.problem: When new evidence reopens a decision recorded under another topic, the arbitrator records a new D-NNN without --reverses, leaving two active ledger entries that disagree.
findings.fix: Pass `PRIOR DECISION: D-NNN` in that case too.

findings.evidence: R3 'position consistency': order_store and order_store_reversed must both pick PostgreSQL with different options shown first. task.md:47-49: 'Both data debates: PostgreSQL. FR-020 needs a multi-row atomic write, and FR-021 needs relational joins' (the document store option is literally 'without multi-document transactions', a brd_alignment anchor-2 conflict with a MUST). The only close call (search_debounce) is run once, in one order; R5 checks that a second opinion exists, not whether it agreed. General LLM-as-judge practice: position bias shows when candidates are close, not when one violates a MUST.
findings.problem: The only measurement of order-robustness, the property the presentation-order shuffle and reversed second opinion exist for, runs on a case position bias can't flip. A prompt or effort change that made the arbitrator order-sensitive on close calls would still score full marks, so /eval --compare can't show the shuffle works or that an effort change helped.
findings.fix: Add search_debounce_reversed with pinned orders (as for order_store) and score agreement between the two verdicts; or run the close call twice per order and score agreement rate.
